description: Open browser URLs when requested, inspect sessions, inspect open apps/windows, bring apps to the main visible screen, and run approved desktop actions for any app through separated macOS, Windows, and Linux drivers. For browser navigation where the user gives an explicit URL, use browser.open_url with that URL before diagnostics or app discovery; do not start with computer.context, computer.apps, or computer.doctor unless browser.open_url fails or no target app/window is known. When the user asks to operate an app with mouse/keyboard, treat browser.open_url or app launch as setup only; verify the visible UI and continue with computer.type/key/click/scroll. Safe computer.type/key/scroll actions try background mode by default when a trusted non-physical background driver is available; if support, permission, or approval is missing, the tool prompts the user before any foreground fallback. For browser UI navigation, prefer show_app/select_window, computer.key command+l, computer.type the user-requested URL or search text, then computer.key return. The computer.type payload text is the literal content to enter; do not type the current URL, app name, or window title unless the user explicitly asked to enter that text. Use computer.apps/windows/show_app/select_window before scoped screenshots or actions, computer.observe for driver-backed inspection of the current visible target, computer.semantic_action for accessibility intents, and computer.doctor only after an observed driver/tool failure that requires diagnostics. For visual clicks, use the zoom ladder: full or selected-window screenshot, crop/zoom the likely region with source=latest when the target is small, then click with normalized_x/normalized_y relative to that attached crop. source=latest crops from the last full/selected-window screenshot; use source=current_crop only when intentionally cropping the current crop again. Take a fresh full/selected-window screenshot before unrelated actions so old zoom coordinates are not reused. Hidden host-window control is disabled; use payload.fallback=foreground only after the user confirms foreground work.

config.name: browser_computer
config.summary: Approved browser and all-app visible-screen computer actions across separated macOS, Windows, and Linux drivers. When the user provides an explicit URL or ordered browser navigation, call browser.open_url for that URL first; reserve computer.context/apps/doctor for missing-target or failure diagnosis. Use computer.show_app to bring Vivaldi/Chrome/etc. to the main screen, computer.select_window for visible windows, and computer.observe for driver-backed target inspection. When the user asks for mouse/keyboard app operation, do not stop after browser.open_url or app launch; inspect the visible UI and continue with computer.type/key/click/scroll. Safe computer.type/key/scroll tries background by default with trusted non-physical drivers; if unavailable, ask foregroundで作業しますか？ and retry with payload.fallback=foreground only after confirmation/approval. Use computer.ocr, computer.ax_tree, and computer.click_text for high-risk read inspection and text-targeted clicks. For browser UI navigation prefer computer.key command+l -> computer.type(user-requested URL/search text) -> computer.key return. The computer.type text is literal input content, not an app name, window title, or current URL unless the user asked for exactly that text. Then use full/selected-window screenshot -> source=latest crop/zoom for small targets -> coordinate_space=normalized_1000 with normalized_x/normalized_y on the attached crop. source=latest crops from the last full/selected-window screenshot; use source=current_crop only for an intentional crop-of-crop. Take a fresh screenshot before unrelated actions so a stale zoom does not trap the model. Use computer.type for text input.

action.description: Use browser.open_url/session for browser navigation and inspection when direct URL opening is the requested step. If the user names a URL such as google.com or youtube.com, choose browser.open_url first and do not choose computer.context, computer.apps, or computer.doctor as the first action unless browser.open_url failed or the target app is unknown. For mouse/keyboard app operation, browser.open_url is setup and must be followed by visible-screen verification and computer.type/key/click/scroll. Safe computer.type/key/scroll try background mode by default; if the result asks foregroundで作業しますか？, do not retry foreground until the user confirms and approval is available, then use payload.fallback=foreground. Use computer.context/apps/windows to inspect open apps only when target state is unknown, computer.show_app to bring an app to the main visible screen, computer.select_window to target a visible window, computer.observe to inspect the current driver chain and visible target state, computer.ocr and computer.ax_tree for high-risk read inspection, computer.click_text with payload text/query/text_query/match_text plus optional element_id/role/confidence_threshold for text-targeted clicks, computer.semantic_action for accessibility-backed intents, computer.pid_event for experimental pid-targeted background-safe actions, and computer.doctor only after a driver/tool failure. For browser UI navigation prefer computer.key key_combo=command+l, computer.type the user-requested URL/search text, then computer.key key=return. Do not use computer.type to enter the app name, window title, or current URL unless the user explicitly requested that literal text. For small or ambiguous image targets, do not click from the full screenshot; request computer.screenshot with crop/zoom/detail first, usually payload.source=latest, then click using payload.normalized_x and payload.normalized_y relative to that attached crop. source=latest crops from the last full/selected-window screenshot; use source=current_crop only for an intentional crop-of-crop. After a zoomed/cropped view, request a fresh screenshot before unrelated actions. payload.point:[y,x] is accepted only for legacy compatibility. computer.click/move/drag default to the virtual AI cursor and marker previews; set payload.physical=true only after explicit approval to operate the visible UI.

payload.description: Action payload. For browser.open_url include url. For computer.show_app/select_app include app/application/name. For computer.type include text: the literal user-requested URL, search query, or form value to enter, not the app name, window title, or current URL unless that is exactly requested. For computer.key include key or key_combo. For visual coordinates, prefer normalized_x and normalized_y plus coordinate_space=normalized_1000. Legacy point:[y,x] and normalized_point are accepted for compatibility only. Use source=latest plus crop, zoom, normalized_box, crop_x/crop_y/crop_width/crop_height, or detail on computer.screenshot to inspect small targets. source=latest crops from the last full/selected-window screenshot; use source=current_crop only when intentionally cropping the current crop again. Cropped/zoomed screenshots become the new attached-image coordinate reference; take a fresh screenshot before unrelated actions. Use app/name with computer.show_app, app/title/title_contains with computer.select_window, key/key_combo with computer.key, text with computer.type, text/query/text_query/match_text plus optional element_id/role/include_ocr/include_ax_tree/confidence_threshold with computer.ocr, computer.ax_tree, or computer.click_text, intent with computer.semantic_action, pid/sub_action with computer.pid_event, and physical=true only when a click/move/drag should operate the visible UI instead of the default virtual marker preview.

window.description: Exact visible-window binding returned by computer.windows/select_window. For background semantic browser-address replacement include app, pid, window_id, x, y, width, and height.

target_control.description: For computer.probe_text_control or computer.type: select the browser address control in the exact nested window. Probe is content-free and read-only; type requests verified background replacement. Both forbid foreground or physical fallback.

background.description: Force a background-only attempt. User-requested computer.type/key/scroll/click defaults to background when safe; if no approved background driver can execute, ask for foreground confirmation or approval before retrying.

foreground.description: Explicitly request foreground execution after user confirmation.

fallback.description: Use foreground only after the user confirms foregroundで作業しますか？ and approval is available.
